question: A farm had 208 acres. They multiplied by 6 to plan expansion. They added 35 acres. They multiplied by 8 to account for all zones. They multiplied by 2 for a comprehensive assessment. Finally, they multiplied by 5 for a full-year projection. Using the word 'twice', how many acres are in the annual land management plan?

A factory started with 236 units. In the morning, production tripled. By midday, they added 58 units. In the afternoon, they added 17 units. By evening, 268 units were removed. Finally, 276 units were removed. How many units remain?

Kim put 25 dollars into her savings jar every week for 7 weeks, then added 74 dollars from her birthday. Her grandfather then doubled whatever was in the jar. A month later her grandmother matched the jar too, so it held twice as much as before her gift. Finally Kim added 30 dollars from babysitting. How many dollars are in Kim's jar now?

A business started with 213 items. They added 10 items. They removed 190 items. They added 58 items. They added 24 items. Finally, they increased 5 times. Converting to hundreds, how many items are there?

Two rival shops compared inventories. Owen's shop had 168 umbrellas in stock, tracked over 240 minutes, or 4 hours, of a busy sale. A supplier's promotion, with seven matching shipments, made his stock eight times as large, even though the shop has a dozen display racks. One umbrella was returned as defective and removed. A late shipment added 79 more umbrellas. A final restock tripled his stock one more time. Owen's shop ended up with far more umbrellas than his rival Cade's shop, which only had 900. How many umbrellas did Owen's shop have at the end?

A farmer started with 52 seeds. They subtracted 34 for planting (morning). They multiplied by 4 through germination counting. They multiplied by 9 for harvest projection. They multiplied by 7 for bulk calculation. Using 'double' as a word quantity and showing time progression through morning/afternoon, how many seeds after subtraction but before the first multiplication?

A gas station tracked the total gallons of fuel in its emergency reserve tank, starting with 59 gallons at dawn. During the morning, a delivery added 10 more gallons. By midday, a generator test used 43 gallons from the tank. In the afternoon, a small leak lost 1 more gallon. By evening, a large delivery added 79 more gallons. Converting the tracked volume from gallons to liters for the corporate report — a simple unit change — the station multiplied the tracked number by 6 that night. How many liters did the tracked reserve show by night?

On Tuesday morning the Sunrise Bakery's first oven turned out 74 loaves, and a second batch from the same oven added 28 loaves. The bakery has 3 identical ovens, and each of the other ovens produced exactly the same morning total as the first. The bakery employs 9 people. In the afternoon the bakers made 13 rye loaves, 59 sourdough loaves, and 56 baguettes on top of the morning's output. In the evening the manager worked out that Tuesday's total was typical, and that the bakery would produce exactly the same total on each of the 7 days of the coming week. How many loaves will the bakery produce over those 7 days?

On Monday morning a bottling plant had 137 crates in the yard, and a delivery brought 46 more. Every crate holds 9 boxes, and each box holds 6 jars. The plant has 3 loading bays, and a dozen staff work on the line. In the afternoon a supermarket bought 2666 jars. That evening 13 jars came back from a damaged pallet. How many jars are in the yard now?

A business had 199 items initially. They removed 128 for delivery. They added 9 from restocking. They multiplied by 4 for expansion. They divided by 2 for equal distribution. The company had 8 locations. How many items per location?

Mae's stationery shop received 7 boxes of pens with 164 pens in each box, more than Nat's shop received. Each pen costs 3 dollars. Mae sold 586 pens in the first month and 422 pens in the second month. She then restocked so that she had 9 pens for every pen left. A supplier sent 63 free pens, and a customer returned 43 pens. How many pens did Mae's shop have?

A base amount was 173 in the morning. By mid-morning, it multiplied by 5. By noon, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, it multiplied by 7 again. By evening, it tripled. How many units was the final amount?

Fay keeps her coins in a jar. She started with 39 cents, then added 70 cents from her grandmother, 38 cents from selling old comics, and 79 cents from returning bottles. She then split the money equally between 2 jars, a blue one and a red one. How many cents are in the blue jar?

A factory had 147 units. They multiplied by 6 to track production. Then by 2 for shift coverage. They added 78 units from extra production. They subtracted 507 units completed. They added 73 units from rework. Finally, 103 units were deducted for quality assurance. Using hours and minutes conversion, what is the final active unit count?

A library had 205 books to catalog. They added 18 books from a donation. They added 65 more books from returns. They doubled for the backup copy system. They removed 315 books that were withdrawn. They added 25 books from a new purchase. How many books were in the final catalog?

Zara is in charge of the flyer stack for the summer festival, and the printer delivered 8 bundles with 171 flyers in each to make up the whole stack. Leo handed out 1135 flyers from the stack on the first day. Zara then printed 6 fresh flyers for every flyer still in the stack and replaced the old ones with them, so the stack held only the new prints. The festival has 4 stages. On the second day Zara handed out 609 flyers herself, far fewer than Leo had managed. For the final weekend she printed enough to make the stack 3 times as large. How many flyers are in the stack now?

A pharmacy records its stock in single bottles rather than in cases, and Salma fills more prescriptions than her colleague Dan does. The shelf held 106 bottles of cough syrup in October, and 61 were dispensed that month. A delivery in November brought 68 more bottles to the shelf. The pharmacy is open 6 days a week. In December 60 bottles were dispensed, and in January a wholesaler sent 46 bottles. How many bottles of cough syrup are on the shelf now?

Linda had 108 dollars on Monday morning. She earned 3 dollars from helping her neighbor. She then earned 8 times that amount from part-time work, giving her significantly more. By Tuesday, she had spent 292 dollars on supplies. She received a check for 78 dollars on Wednesday. She then split her remaining funds equally in half. How much was each half?

A store started with 76 toys in inventory. They multiplied stock by 9 for restocking. They added 64 toys from a supplier delivery. They added 35 more toys in the evening. They added 22 toys from returns. They removed 622 toy units for a recall. The store manager worked 40 hours a week. How many toys remained on the shelves?

A farmers market tracked the total pounds of apples at the orchard stand throughout the day, starting with 136 pounds at opening. During the morning, a delivery added 52 more pounds. By midday, another delivery added 53 more pounds. A dozen market vendors set up nearby, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked apple weight. In the afternoon, a bulk order doubled the tracked apple weight after a matching donation came in. A separate stand selling pears, unrelated to this one, had 90 pounds. By evening, a final delivery added 71 more pounds. How many pounds of apples did the tracked stand have by evening?

A print shop tracked the total flyers on the press run, starting with 107 flyers. A test batch removed 35 flyers for quality checks. A dozen new ink cartridges were installed that morning, though that number has nothing to do with the flyer count. A full production run then multiplied the tracked flyer count by 6. A big client order removed 282 flyers from the tracked total. A second client added 78 more flyers back into the tracked run. A third client added 46 more. Finally, a damaged batch removed 197 flyers from the tracked total. A separate press run, unrelated to this one, produced 500 flyers. How many flyers were in the tracked run at the end?

A farm had 134 chickens initially. They removed 124 chickens for harvest. They added 8 chickens from new breeding. They multiplied by 3 to calculate egg production. They tripled again for the quarterly forecast. There were 156 ducks (not counted). How many chickens were in the annual projection?

Two food banks compared their canned goods. Riverside Food Bank had 195 cans, even though it has a dozen volunteers on staff. The cans were split evenly among 3 storage rooms, and only one room's cans were counted going forward. A shipment error meant 31 cans had to be discarded, out of the 500 cans donated citywide that month. A donation drive then added 62 more cans. A matching grant from five community partners made the room's count six times as large. Finally, 390 cans were sent out to shelters, leaving Riverside Food Bank well behind the rival Lakeside Food Bank's 700 cans. How many cans did Riverside Food Bank have left?

A bakery started with 54 items (morning start). They added 29 (morning). They doubled (multiplied by 2, morning/afternoon). They subtracted 28 for spoilage (mid-afternoon). They multiplied by 9 for batch calculation. They multiplied by 4 for scaling (evening, using 'double' as word quantity). 'One distractor': competitor made 500 items. After addition and doubling but before spoilage, how many items in the afternoon?

A musician had 23 songs. They multiplied by 6 times. They removed 13 songs. They removed 43 songs. They added 12 songs. Morning composing, afternoon arranging, evening mastering. Someone had a dozen songs. How many songs?
